subtopics.title: Forces Are Interactions — the Cast Around the Box

questions.question: The weight of the 5 kg box (using g = 9,8 m/s²) is:
options: 5 N downward
9,8 N downward
49 N downward
49 kg downward

questions.question: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: They are two names for the same thing
Mass is the amount of matter (a scalar); weight is the gravitational force on it (a vector)
Weight is measured in kilograms
Mass changes on the Moon; weight does not

questions.question: The test for whether a force belongs on the diagram is:
options: Does the object move in that direction?
Is the force bigger than 1 newton?
Is the force horizontal or vertical?
Can you name the object responsible for the push or pull?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a real force on the sliding box?
options: The normal force from the floor
A forward 'force of motion' keeping it moving
The weight from the Earth
Friction from the rough floor

questions.question: In a free-body diagram, the object is represented as:
options: A detailed sketch including the floor and rope
A single dot with all force arrows starting from it
A circle containing the force values
An arrow showing its velocity

questions.question: The applied force arrow for our box must be drawn:
options: Straight up
Horizontally forward
At 30° above the horizontal, with the angle clearly marked
At 30° below the horizontal

questions.question: Friction on the forward-sliding box is drawn:
options: Vertically downward
In the same direction as the pull
At 30° below the horizontal
Horizontally backward, opposing the sliding

questions.question: Which item would COST marks if included in a free-body diagram?
options: A velocity arrow drawn as if it were a force
A labelled weight arrow
The marked 30° angle
An arrowhead on each force

subtopics.title: Reading the Physics Off the Diagram — Constant Velocity

questions.question: 'Constant velocity' tells you that:
options: The applied force is the largest force
The net force on the box is zero — all forces balance (Newton's first law)
Friction is zero
The box is accelerating slowly

questions.question: The horizontal balance for the box reads:
options: $F_{applied} = f$
$F_{applied}\sin 30° = f$
$F_{applied}\cos 30° = f$
$N = w$

questions.question: Why is the normal force LESS than 49 N in this problem?
options: The box is moving, which always reduces the normal force
Friction cancels part of the weight
It is not less — N always equals w
The rope's vertical component ($F_{applied}\sin 30°$) helps lift the box, so the floor pushes less

questions.question: Why does pulling at an upward angle make a box easier to drag (in later grades)?
options: A smaller normal force means less friction, since friction depends on the normal force
The box weighs less when pulled
Angles always increase the applied force
Friction acts upward when the rope is angled

subtopics.title: The Method, the Error Museum, and the Road Ahead

questions.question: The systematic hunt for forces on an object starts with:
options: The fastest-moving object nearby
Friction
Gravity (always present), then every object touching the body
The applied force

questions.question: Friction always opposes:
options: The applied force, whatever its direction
The relative sliding between the surfaces
The weight
The normal force

questions.question: A free-body diagram must show forces:
options: Exerted BY the object on its surroundings
On every object in the problem at once
Acting ON the chosen object only — one object per diagram
Only the two largest forces

subtopics.title: Who Is Actually Pulling on the Box?

questions.question: Dragging a gas bottle across a yard, which four objects act on it?
options: The Earth, the ground, the rope and the rough surface
The Earth, the air, the sun and the rope
The rope only
The Earth and the person's momentum

questions.question: Weight equals mass times gravitational acceleration. For the 5 kg box that is:
options: 5 N
49 N, straight down

questions.question: Which statement about mass and weight is correct?
options: Both are measured in newtons
Both would be unchanged on the Moon
Mass stays 5 kg on the Moon; the weight becomes smaller because the Moon pulls more gently
Weight stays 49 N on the Moon; the mass becomes smaller

questions.question: Why is there no 'force of moving forward' on the sliding box?
options: Because it is too small to matter
Because it acts only at high speed
Because friction already cancels it
Because no object supplies it — moving is something the box does, not something done to it

questions.question: What is thrown away when a force diagram becomes a free-body diagram?
options: The force arrows
The scenery — floor, rope and box outline — leaving a dot and the arrows
The labels on the arrows
The angles

questions.question: Said out loud, the four arrows leaving the dot are:
options: Up, up, left and right
Down, up, backwards and downwards
Down for weight, up for the normal force, slanted forward and up for the rope, backwards for friction
Only the rope and the weight

questions.question: An arrow without an arrowhead is a problem because:
options: It has not shown a direction, which is half of what a force is
It looks untidy
It makes the diagram too long
Arrowheads are optional

questions.question: Which one belongs on the free-body diagram?
options: The floor, sketched under the dot
The rope, drawn up to a hand
An arrow showing how fast the box is moving
A labelled arrow for the normal force, starting at the dot

subtopics.title: Why the Slant Helps — and What "Constant Speed" Is Telling You

questions.question: 'Constant speed in a straight line' is the examiner telling you that:
options: The rope is the strongest force
Forward and backward effects are equal, and up and down effects are equal — nothing is winning
Friction has stopped acting
The box is about to stop

questions.question: Pulling a wheeled suitcase by its handle does two jobs at once. In physics those two jobs are called:
options: Two separate forces from two ropes
Weight and normal force
The horizontal component and the vertical component of one force
Friction and tension

questions.question: The up-and-down balance for the box, in words, is:
options: The floor's push plus the rope's upward part equals the weight
The floor's push equals the weight, always
The weight plus the rope's upward part equals the floor's push
The friction equals the weight

questions.question: Why is dragging a heavy bag by a strap slanted up over your shoulder easier than dragging it flat?
options: The bag loses mass when lifted
Straps are stronger than hands
Friction disappears when the bag is tilted
The upward pull lightens the floor's push, and less normal force means less friction
